title: A slice of stars
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 3501, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3501 · constellation Leo · about 80 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A thin, glowing streak slices across this Hubble image, with only a few foreground stars and distant background galaxies for company. It is NGC 3501, a spiral galaxy seen edge-on, which gives it a long, very narrow look.

It is not as lonely as it appears. Just out of frame is its companion, NGC 3507, and the two travel through space together as a pair. They look very different from each other, which again comes down to perspective, since NGC 3507 is seen face-on, showing off its barred, swirling arms.

NGC 3501 is also a spiral, though a different kind from its partner. It has no bar through its center. Instead, its loosely wound arms all start from the middle. Seen from the side, those arms appear as bright gas and stars glowing along the streak, mottled by dark lanes of dust that run across the galaxy.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.33 x 3.13 arcminutes) and distance (80 million light years), the frame spans roughly 77,000 × 73,000 light-years. Its light set out about 80 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and combines visible and near-infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail by eye, and part of the data is near-infrared light, which the eye cannot detect.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA Acknowledgement: Nick Rose
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Contestant Nick Rose submitted a version of this picture to Hubble's Hidden Treasures image processing competition. The finished picture shows how much detail the galaxy's thin edge still holds.
alt: A thin, glowing edge-on galaxy slicing across a dark field with a few stars and small background galaxies.
